newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine reiterates no relief for tax dodgers.
newsitem.headline: Argentine reiterates no relief for tax dodgers.

text.p: Argentina's Economy Ministry reiterated Monday that there will be no relief for workers who do not pay their taxes.

In the second press release on the issue in four days, the ministry stated the government "will not introduce any kind of measure that would benefit those that do not or have not paid their taxes and pension liabilities."
The ministry added that the tax authorities are working to impose charges of two percent monthly on delayed payments.
Any form of disincentive to pay taxes "will be vetoed by the government," said the statement.

The first statement last Thursday came two days after Labor Minister Armando Caro Figueroa suggested the government was planning a blanket amnesty for employers will illegal workers, according to local press reports.

The ministry has made the tax evasion fight a central policy issue. The government estimates that $20 billion in taxes are dodged every year - equivalent to half the country's annual public expenditure.
Cracking down on evasion has become especially important because of the uphill struggle in plugging the budget deficit.
